items.title: Risk-weighted apoB and lipoprotein-associated coronary risk across ethnic groups.
items.abstract: Apolipoprotein B (apoB) reflects the number of circulating atherogenic lipoproteins but does not account for differences in particle atherogenicity. Risk-weighted apoB (RW-apoB), which incorporates triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)), may better capture lipoprotein-driven coronary risk, but its performance across diverse populations remains uncertain. We assessed whether the prespecified triglyceride - and Lp(a)-weighted information captured by RW-apoB was associated with coronary events beyond apoB and compared the discrimination of RW-apoB and measured apoB across ethnicities. We analyzed 40,132 participants with 4,509 coronary events from ARIC, CARDIA, MESA, the Framingham Offspring Study, and China Kadoorie Biobank. RW-apoB was calculated using a prespecified equation. Mutually adjusted Cox estimates were pooled within ethnic groups using random-effects meta-analysis. Separate single-marker models compared discrimination. Sensitivity analyses included age and sex adjustment, standardized exposures, hard-events, truncated follow-up, and CKB-specific logistic regression. Mean RW-apoB exceeded apoB by approximately 8 mg/dL in African American and Chinese participants, reflecting higher lipoprotein(a) and triglycerides, respectively. RW-apoB was associated with coronary events conditional on apoB in White, African American, Chinese, and Hispanic participants: hazard ratios per 10 mg/dL were 1.11 (95% CI 1.05-1.18), 1.11 (1.08-1.15), 1.08 (1.05-1.11), and 1.10 (1.01-1.21), respectively. C-indices for RW-apoB versus apoB were 0.630 versus 0.617 in White (P<0.001), 0.606 versus 0.595 in African American (P=0.085), 0.567 versus 0.554 in Chinese (P=0.014), and 0.540 versus 0.535 in Hispanic participants (P=0.756). RW-apoB captured lipoprotein-associated risk beyond measured apoB, with discrimination gains statistically demonstrable in the larger White and Chinese groups. A measure combining apolipoprotein B (apoB) with triglycerides and lipoprotein(a), termed risk-weighted apoB (RW-apoB), provided additional information about coronary heart disease risk beyond apoB alone, although its value for routine clinical risk prediction remains to be established. Among more than 40,000 participants from diverse populations, differences between RW-apoB and apoB mainly reflected higher lipoprotein(a) in African American participants and higher triglycerides in Chinese participants. RW-apoB was associated with coronary events after accounting for apoB. Its ability to distinguish participants with earlier events was modestly higher than that of apoB in all four groups, with statistically significant improvements only demonstrable in the larger, White and Chinese groups.

items.title: Beyond the Gradient: Patient-Reported Outcomes with Aficamten in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
Cellular consequences of non-ablative radiotherapy, a novel approach to ventricular tachycardias.
items.abstract: Radiotherapy (RT) with a single application of ionizing radiation (STAR) has been suggested as a non-invasive alternative to radiofrequency in ablating ventricular tachycardia (VT). Emerging data reveal that STAR may suppress VT without substrate destruction, by enhancing impulse conduction instead, through increased expression of NaV1.5 channels and connexin 43. The study aims to investigate electrophysiology and intracellular Ca2+ dynamics in cardiomyocytes (CMs) from mice subjected to in-vivo RT. The emerging data led us to evaluate biochemical changes potentially linking electrophysiological response to ionizing irradiation. CMs isolated 2 weeks after RT with low-dose (15 Gy) or high-dose (25 Gy) were compared to those of sham-treated mice (CTRL). We evaluated: i) the properties of the transient (INaT) and sustained (INasus) components of INa; ii) AP parameters, including the prevalence of Early After-Depolarizations (EADs); iii) intracellular Ca2+ dynamics; iv) CaMKII phosphorylation and v) ROS content. 25 Gy RT i) increased INaT and, to a larger extent, INasus (increased INasus/INaT ratio); ii) increased AP amplitude, +dV/dtMAX and duration (APD) and facilitated EADs; iii) depressed intracellular Ca2+ dynamics. 15 Gy RT had similar but smaller effects (dose-dependency). 25 Gy RT reduced CaMKII phosphorylation but increased cell ROS content, thus providing a mechanism for the late component of INa (INaL) enhancement. The results support the view that STAR may supress VT by increasing conduction velocity, with APD prolongation providing an additional mechanism. On the other hand, INasus enhancement and Ca2+ handling depression may impair electrical stability and contractility in the irradiated region.

items.title: Impact of Photon-Counting CT Acquisition Modes on Coronary Stenosis Assessment and Radiation Dose: A Phantom and Clinical Evaluation.
items.abstract: Photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCD-CT) offers high spatial resolution and dose-efficient coronary CT angiography (cCTA), but protocol selection, especially optimal acquisition mode, requires balancing spacial resolution, temporal robustness and radiation exposure. This study evaluated various PCD-CT acquisition modes in terms of image quality, blooming, stenosis grading, diagnostic accuracy, and radiation dose using phantom and clinical cCTA. First-generation dual-source PCD-CT was used with four acquisition modes: high-pitch spiral with prospective ECG-gating (Flash), Sequence, Spiral, and retrospective ultra-high-resolution (UHR) spiral mode. Phantom experiments used six 3D-printed coronary artery models with stenoses ranging from 21% to 73%. In a retrospective clinical study, 41 cCTA examinations were analyzed. Qualitative and quantitative image assessments used invasive coronary angiography as reference standard for diagnostic accuracy. Patient characteristics and radiation doses were recorded. UHR demonstrated the highest image quality and the lowest quantitative blooming in phantom and clinical data (clinical image quality score: UHR 4.12 ± 0.99 vs. Flash 3.00 ± 0.86; p = 0.002). Diagnostic accuracy varied across protocols for detecting ≥50% and ≥70% stenoses was high across all modes (e.g., Flash: 76.5% each; Sequence: 100% and 57.1%; UHR: 64.7% and 82.4%). Radiation dose was highest in UHR (26.44 ± 9.76 mSv) compared with Sequence (13.65 ± 8.86 mSv) and Flash (1.40 ± 0.32 mSv); all p ≤ 0.011. While UHR acquisition provides highest image quality in PCD-CT cCTA, lower-dose acquisition modes achieve comparable diagnostic accuracy for coronary stenosis detection. Protocol selection should therefore be individualized, and prospective controlled studies are required.

items.title: Prognostic impact of coronary artery ectasia after acute coronary syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Coronary artery ectasia (CAE) is associated with abnormal coronary flow, thrombus formation, and impaired reperfusion, but its prognostic significance after acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains uncertain. To evaluate clinical outcomes among patients with versus without CAE presenting with ACS. PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched from inception to April 2026 for studies comparing ACS patients with versus without CAE. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Subgroup, leave-one-out, and Bayesian random-effects analyses were performed to assess robustness. Twelve observational studies comprising 13,540 patients were analyzed, including 1177 with CAE and 12,363 without CAE. Follow-up ranged from in-hospital assessment to 120 months. CAE was associated with a higher risk of recurrent myocardial infarction (RR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.16-3.32; P = 0.022; I 2  = 61.1%), corresponding to an estimated absolute excess of 58.6 events per 1000 patients and a descriptive number needed to harm of 17. For stroke, the prespecified Hartung-Knapp analysis yielded an RR of 2.40 (95% CI, 1.59-3.61), whereas conventional random-effects inference, used as the basis of interpretation, yielded an RR of 2.40 (95% CI, 1.08-5.31; P = 0.031). This estimate was based on 3 studies and was model-sensitive. CAE was not significantly associated with all-cause mortality, in-hospital mortality, cardiac death, repeat revascularization, or MACE. Stent thrombosis was not pooled because only 2 studies provided estimable stent-exposed comparisons. Bayesian analyses supported the recurrent myocardial infarction finding. Among patients presenting with ACS, CAE identifies a higher-risk ischemic phenotype, with the most consistent association observed for recurrent myocardial infarction. Prospective studies are needed to define CAE-specific risk stratification and treatment strategies.

items.title: Cardiovascular Toxicities of Contemporary Cancer Immunotherapies: A Narrative Review of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors, Bispecific T-Cell Engagers, and CAR-T Cell Therapies.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), bispecific T-cell engagers (BiTEs), and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapies have produced durable responses across different hematologic malignancies, but each class carries cardiovascular liabilities that differ fundamentally in mechanism, incidence, timing, and mortality risk. A structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE and EMBASE from inception through March 2026 was performed, supplemented by pharmacovigilance data from FAERS and WHO VigiBase, to review and synthesize the available evidence on cardiovascular toxicity and provide a structured comparison of incidence, mechanisms, clinical presentation, outcomes, and monitoring strategies to guide clinical practice. ICI-associated myocarditis is rare (0.06%-1.14%) but carries a case fatality rate approaching 50%, a lethality amplified by combination regimens and obscured by preserved left ventricular ejection fraction in approximately half of presentations. BiTEs may occupy a mechanistically intermediate position: cardiovascular adverse events are reported in 8% to 20% of pharmacovigilance cases, and 83% of these arise without documented concurrent cytokine release syndrome (CRS), implying that their immunopathological profile lies closer to ICI than to CAR-T injury. Bispecific agents are not a homogeneous class: blinatumomab, teclistamab, talquetamab, and elranatamab differ in construct, target antigen, disease setting, CRS frequency, and reported cardiovascular phenotype, and agent-level effects cannot presently be separated from population-level ones. CAR-T cell therapy produces cardiovascular events in up to 19% to 26% of patients, predominantly through IL-6-driven, CRS-coupled hemodynamic injury, with left ventricular dysfunction resolving in the majority following CRS management. Across all 3 classes, foundational clinical trials incorporated no routine cardiac monitoring, current surveillance practices are heterogeneous, and no prospective head-to-head comparative data exist. Each immune therapy class poses a qualitatively distinct cardiac threat at a different point in the treatment course. Risk-adapted surveillance extending beyond the CRS window appears prudent for BiTEs, although this reflects extrapolation rather than validated evidence; serologic and imaging monitoring regardless of systemic symptoms remains essential for ICI recipients; and CRS-guided early intervention is the cornerstone of CAR-T cardiotoxicity management. This review aims to provide clinicians with a comprehensive overview of the cardiovascular toxicities associated with these modern therapies.

items.title: IFM 2026 Recommendations for First-line Treatment of Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma.
items.abstract: The treatment landscape of newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM) has changed considerably over the past 5 years. Anti-CD38-VRd quadruplets are now the standard of care for transplant-eligible patients and an important option for transplant-ineligible patients. This review presents unified, evidence-based first-line treatment recommendations from the Intergroupe Francophone du Myélome (IFM), covering transplant-eligible and transplant-ineligible NDMM within a single framework and common methodology. In transplant-eligible patients, daratumumab-VRd and isatuximab-VRd, informed respectively by the PERSEUS and GMMG-HD7 trials, are now the reference induction regimens, followed by autologous stem cell transplantation, optional consolidation, and daratumumab-lenalidomide maintenance. In transplant-ineligible patients, daratumumab-lenalidomide-dexamethasone (DRd), informed by the MAIA trial, remains the treatment backbone: in fit patients, adding bortezomib (isatuximab-VRd or daratumumab-VRd, informed by IMROZ, CEPHEUS, and BENEFIT) could further improve outcomes, while frail patients receive the same backbone without dexamethasone (DR), informed by IFM2017-03. Mathematical modeling projects a median progression-free survival of approximately 205 months with daratumumab-VRd in transplant-eligible patients (PERSEUS model) and approximately 100 months in transplant-ineligible/transplant-deferred patients (CEPHEUS model), approaching for the first time a normal life expectancy for a substantial subset of patients and supporting the emerging concept of functional cure. We discuss the role of measurable residual disease and NGS-based high-risk myeloma definition across both populations, and position these recommendations relative to the 2025 EHA-EMN evidence-based guidelines. Finally, we summarize ongoing trials investigating T-cell-redirecting immunotherapies (CAR-T cells and bispecific antibodies) as replacements for, or additions to, ASCT and maintenance therapy, which may further reshape the first-line treatment paradigm in the coming years.

Verbascoside inhibits ovarian cancer proliferation via IRAK4-CXCL5 axis-mediated suppression of neutrophil infiltration and neutrophil extracellular trap formation.
items.abstract: The specific mechanisms of Verbascoside (VB) in ovarian cancer (OC) remain insufficient. This study aimed to explore the anti-tumor mechanisms of VB in OC, focusing on its ability to modulate the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), particularly through targeting neutrophil infiltration and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). The anti-tumor and anti-NETosis efficacy of VB was evaluated in vivo using subcutaneous, orthotopic, and pulmonary metastasis mouse models of OC. Microproteomics and bioinformatics analysis identified the direct molecular target of VB and the key neutrophil chemoattractant. The underlying mechanisms were validated in vitro and in vivo (using SKOV3, ID8, and neutrophils), alongside loss-of-function approaches. The combination of VB with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy was also assessed. VB inhibited OC proliferation/metastasis, promoted anti-tumor immunity, and suppressed neutrophil infiltration and NETosis. Neutrophil depletion attenuated VB's anti-metastatic effect. Microproteomics and bioinformatics screening identified IRAK4 as a direct molecular target of VB and CXCL5 as a key neutrophil chemoattractant. SPR confirmed the direct binding between VB and IRAK4, and molecular docking revealed specific hydrogen bond interactions. Mechanistically, VB treatment or IRAK4 knockdown suppressed CXCL5 expression, and consequently reduced neutrophil infiltration and NETosis. Consistently, CXCL5 overexpression abrogated the inhibitory effects of VB on neutrophil NETosis and recruitment. Furthermore, VB synergized with anti-PD-1 therapy, thereby achieving superior tumor growth inhibition, reduced Ki67 expression, and enhanced CD8 + T cell infiltration. In conclusion, VB exerts potent anti-tumor effects in OC by targeting the IRAK4/CXCL5 axis, thereby inhibiting neutrophil infiltration and NETosis, reshaping the immunosuppressive TME, and restoring anti-tumor immunity.

items.title: Preventing cancer Down Under: Australian screening guidelines for prevention of anal cancer in people living with HIV: the pathologists' viewpoint.
items.abstract: Anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) is a human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cancer with a rising incidence. People living with human immunodeficiency virus (PLHIV) are at the highest risk. Recent evidence has shown that treatment of the precursor lesion, high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), can prevent cancer development. Consequently, several countries have published screening guidelines for anal HSIL as a strategy to decrease cancer incidence. In Australia, the Australasian Society for HIV, Viral Hepatitis and Sexual Health Medicine (ASHM) has recently released guidelines for PLHIV, based on HPV testing and genotyping, with liquid-based cytology (LBC) used as a triage tool for those testing positive to high-risk HPV. The pathologist's role will be critical to the success of this endeavour. This article describes the scientific basis for the recommended screening algorithm. The key features of each testing component are outlined, including anal swab collection, biopsy interpretation and the importance of relevant clinical information, to enhance communication between pathologist and clinician. Future developments are discussed, including the possibility of extension of the benefits of such screening to other at-risk groups.

items.title: Research news in clinical context.
Hepatitis B Guinea-Bissau trial: Researchers behind controversial study weigh in as confusion reigns over its fate.
Numerous linked cases of acute genotype F hepatitis B virus infections in people living with HIV or on pre-exposure prophylaxis.
items.abstract: At least 2.7 million people living with HIV are infected with HBV worldwide. Some antiretroviral treatments and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-based Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) protect against HBV infection. However, emerging antiretroviral (ARV) strategies without any activity against HBV may promote spread of this virus in the future. In this context, we studied recent cases of acute HBV infection in people at risk of sexually transmitted infections. Our objective was to better understand HBV circulation and the dynamics of its transmission. This retrospective study included people diagnosed with acute hepatitis B virus infections between 2022 and 2025 in France. The whole HBV genome was amplified and sequenced by NGS for network analysis. Sixteen men, with a median age of 35 years, were enrolled. Six were living with HIV, including three receiving long-acting injectable cabotegravir/rilpivirine treatment. Four of the HIV-negative individuals were taking PrEP. Nine had been vaccinated against HBV, and six had anti-HBs antibody titers between 10 and 100 IU/L. Analysis revealed HBV genotype F1b in 14 patients, with very high homology among the viruses. No known immune escape mutations were identified, even in the individuals with anti-HBs antibodies. A transmission cluster of HBV F1b genotype was observed in a population at risk of infection. This genotype, which is endemic to Latin Ameria, is rarely detected in France. These findings may serve as a timely reminder of the ongoing circulation of HBV among exposed populations. HBV transmission among vaccinated individuals with positive anti-HBs antibodies raises questions and should be further studied.

items.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma in Turkey: A nationwide health system database analysis of clinical patterns and survival.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. However, comprehensive population-level data describing etiologic patterns, treatment exposure, healthcare utilisation, and survival remain limited in many countries. This study aimed to characterise the national burden, care patterns, and outcomes of HCC in Turkey. We performed a nationwide, real-world analysis of adult patients diagnosed with HCC between 2016 and 2024 using administrative health data. Cases were identified by an administrative case definition requiring at least three separate records of ICD-10 codes C22, C22.0, or C22.9; at least one C22.0 code was not required, so HCC could not be confirmed at the individual level. Baseline comorbidities were restricted to conditions recorded on or before the date of diagnosis. Demographic characteristics, underlying liver disease, etiologic factors, treatment exposure, and the level and type of diagnosing institution were assessed. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. To reduce immortal-time bias, treatment exposure was analysed in a three-month landmark cohort; because treatment dates were unavailable, this reduces but does not eliminate the bias. Multivariable Cox regression was performed within the same cohort. A total of 13,674 patients (64.6% male; median age 64 years, IQR 55-73) were included, of whom 61.4% had died at the data cutoff; median follow-up was 53.0 months. The median OS was 13.2 months (95% CI 12.1-14.5), with 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS of 50.9%, 41.1%, and 36.9%; because patients dying before three qualifying records accumulated could not enter the cohort, these estimates apply to patients meeting the case-identification algorithm and are likely to overstate population survival. OS was markedly longer in women than in men (median 50.9 vs 8.2 months), and longer in patients without cirrhosis recorded at diagnosis than in those with cirrhosis (18.5 vs 9.0 months; both P < 0.001). Hepatitis B was the most frequently recorded specific etiology (29.4%); among mutually exclusive categories, NAFLD-associated HCC had the most favourable survival (5-year OS 61.0%) and alcohol-related HCC the least (median 8.8 months), while HBV-HDV co-infection was associated with longer survival than HBV mono-infection (58.2 vs 12.0 months; P < 0.001), a difference that persisted after adjustment for age, sex, and cirrhosis; no specific etiology could be assigned in 56.1% of patients. Sensitivity analyses restricting etiologic ascertainment to codes recorded within 3 months before to 3 months after diagnosis, or incorporating viral serology, attenuated the survival of the specific viral etiologies, indicating survival-dependent ascertainment. In a multivariable Cox model fitted in the three-month landmark cohort (n = 8958), older age, male sex, cirrhosis, and systemic therapy were associated with higher mortality (all P < 0.001), with time-varying associations for age, cirrhosis, and systemic therapy. The association of local therapy with mortality was not constant over follow-up (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.72-0.85 during 0-24 months after the landmark and 1.22, 1.04-1.43 thereafter); the overall association was no longer evident after liver transplantation was excluded from the local-therapy category. Care was highly centralised within secondary and tertiary institutions. In this nationwide analysis, HCC in Turkey was characterised by limited OS and pronounced sex-based disparities, with survival differing by cirrhosis status and recorded etiology; etiologic ascertainment was itself survival-dependent, so these contrasts describe recorded categories. Hepatitis B was the most frequently recorded specific etiology, underscoring the continued importance of HBV prevention, screening, and surveillance, while HCV, HDV, alcohol-related and metabolic liver disease accounted for smaller recorded proportions; temporal trends in etiology were not analysed. Because tumour stage and liver function were unavailable, the treatment-survival associations are descriptive and subject to confounding by indication. Efforts focused on HBV control, earlier detection, risk-based surveillance of patients with cirrhosis, and improved referral pathways may improve population-level outcomes.

items.title: A practical AI model for endoscopic diagnosis of gastric premalignant lesions and its application to predicting metachronous recurrence.
items.abstract: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based optical system for chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) and intestinal metaplasia (IM), and its ability to predict metachronous recurrence. We analyzed 72,794 endoscopic images from 5,000 patients undergoing esophagogastroduodenoscopy with biopsy-confirmed CAG/IM. A convolutional neural network model was developed and compared with experts (n=16) and novices (n=15). The association between AI-predicted IM extent and metachronous recurrence after endoscopic resection of early gastric cancer (n=458) was evaluated using Cox regression. For CAG, the AI model achieved accuracies of 0.819 (antrum) and 0.864 (body), with corresponding AUCs of 0.885 and 0.901. For IM, accuracies were 0.759 and 0.723, with AUCs of 0.835 and 0.744. The AI model outperformed novices and experts in CAG diagnosis (accuracy: 0.855 vs. 0.705 and 0.751) and outperformed novices in IM diagnosis (0.875 vs. 0.781). Although individual HRs for AI-predicted IM extent were not statistically significant (2.11 [95% CI, 0.25-17.67], antral IM only; 4.27 [0.57-31.97], IM extending to body), a significant dose-response relationship with recurrence risk was observed (P trend =0.043). This AI model showed clinically acceptable performance and potential usefulness for CAG/IM diagnosis in a single-center study but requires multicenter external validation before clinical adoption.

items.title: A robust biomarker combining radiomic and CA19.9 information to predict distant relapse-free survival after radiochemotherapy in pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: The radiomic feature Statistical Percentile 10% (p10%), extracted from [¹⁸F]FDG-PET images, has been previously identified and validated as a robust predictor of distant progression-free survival (DPFS) in unresectable pancreatic cancer (LAPC). This study aimed to maximize its prognostic potential by combining p10% with CA19.9 serum levels and assessing its generalizability across distinct clinical settings. We analyzed 287 LAPC patients treated with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and a validation cohort of 72 patients enrolled in the CASSANDRA trial (resectable/borderline-resectable PDAC). Cox models combined p10% with CA19.9 levels measured before RT in LAPC patients, and before surgery for CASSANDRA patients. p10% was independently prognostic in both cohorts and its integration with CA19.9 significantly improved the prediction. In the LAPC cohort, the combined model achieved C-index=0.71, with median DPFS of 4.0-vs-15.0 months (p<0.0001;HR=3.22). In the pre-surgery setting (CASSANDRA trial), the model showed good rank-order discrimination (C-index=0.65), with median survival of 11.6 months vs not-reached (p=0.0018). However, the calibration slope of 0.54 suggests that absolute risk prediction requires recalibration in the surgical cohort. Integrating p10% with CA19.9 provides a broader representation of tumor aggressiveness. The combined biomarkers demonstrate consistent performance across different disease stages supporting their use for treatment personalization.

items.title: Real-World Germline Variant Landscape and Clinical Management in Korean Patients Tested for Suspected Hereditary Cancer.
items.abstract: Germline pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants inform cancer treatment and prevention, yet real-world detection patterns and downstream clinical management remain poorly characterized in East Asian hereditary cancer cohorts. This retrospective cohort study included 5829 patients with cancer who underwent germline testing at the National Cancer Center, Republic of Korea, between April 2006 and April 2023 using BRCA1/2-only testing or multigene panel testing. We examined P/LP variant prevalence, detection patterns under the revised national reimbursement criteria, gene group-stratified post-test clinical management, and variant reclassification outcomes. Among 5829 patients (96.6% female; median age, 51 years), 987 (16.9%) carried P/LP variants. Detection rates differed across reimbursement criteria, with the highest rates in patients with ovarian cancer (24.2%) and those meeting multiple criteria (up to 39.3%). Among P/LP carriers, 773 (78.3%) received at least one post-test clinical action; however, action rates differed substantially across gene groups, ranging from 84.3% among BRCA1/2 carriers to 46.0% among mismatch repair gene carriers. Of 1384 initial variants of uncertain significance, 25 (1.8%) were reclassified as P/LP, identifying 46 additional carriers. Overall variant frequencies were strongly shaped by the breast and ovarian cancer-predominant cohort composition, whereas documented post-test clinical actions varied across gene groups. Variant reclassification identified additional P/LP carriers, supporting the need for structured recontact and follow-up pathways.

items.title: Profiling circulating tumor DNA for recurrence prediction and prevention in hepatocellular carcinoma following liver transplantation.
items.abstract: Sensitive biomarkers for recurrence risk stratification, recurrence surveillance and adjuvant therapy guidance are of unmet need for patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) undergoing liver transplantation (LT). Herein, we explored the potential of profiling circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for prediction and prevention of recurrence in HCC after LT. HCC patients (n=91) who underwent LT were prospectively enrolled. ctDNA was assayed using next-generation sequencing from perioperative plasma (n=408). Associations between ctDNA status with clinicopathological parameters, tumor recurrence, and adjuvant treatment effect were analyzed. Higher preoperative ctDNA burden correlated with microvascular invasion (median: 45.0 vs 5.1 MTM/mL, P=0.003) and recurrence (156.2 vs 7.7 MTM/mL, P<0.001). ctDNA clearance was noted in 87.7% patients after LT and patients who kept positive postoperative ctDNA showed higher recurrence risk (HR=8.86, P<0.001), especially early recurrence (within 1 year; 75.0% vs 10.1%, P<0.001). During follow-up, positive longitudinal ctDNA was similarly predictive of recurrence (HR=36.50, P<0.001). The AUC of longitudinal ctDNA for predicting recurrence was 0.930-significantly higher than alpha-fetoprotein (0.655, P<0.001). Longitudinal ctDNA detected radiologically evidenced recurrence with a median lead time of 5.1 months compared to standard-of-care surveillance. Among patients who received adjuvant therapy, those with positive postoperative ctDNA could benefit (HR=0.11, P=0.003) and those with decreased ctDNA burden following treatment experienced longer interval from ctDNA positivity to recurrence (HR=0.17, P=0.006). Serial ctDNA analysis demonstrates strong prognostic value, capable of heralding tumor recurrence prior to radiological recurrence and measuring treatment efficacy. Its integration into clinical practice of HCC provides unique opportunities for adjuvant therapy decision-making following LT.

items.title: Long non-coding RNA LINC00885 contributes to liver steatosis through modulation of DHRS2-associated lipid metabolic programs.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent and rising liver disease. Its inflammatory subtype, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), can progress to fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. The role of long intergenic non-protein coding RNA 885 (LINC00885) in MASLD remains unknown. This study aims to clarify its function in steatotic liver disease. Public liver transcriptomic datasets, RNA sequencing of LINC00885-knockdown Hep G2 cells, and microarray profiling under lipotoxic conditions were integrated to identify candidate downstream components. Gain- and loss-of-function models, Oil Red O staining, RT-qPCR, an actinomycin D chase assay, functional rescue, and JC-1 analysis were used to evaluate the LINC00885-DHRS2 axis. Circulating exosomal RNA and exploratory ROC analyses were assessed in a pilot cohort. LINC00885 was upregulated in MASH liver tissue and induced by FFA treatment in hepatocytes. LINC00885 promoted lipid accumulation and shifted lipid metabolic gene expression toward lipogenesis. Integrated transcriptomic analyses identified DHRS2 as a convergent downstream candidate. LINC00885 knockdown increased DHRS2 expression and was associated with slower DHRS2 mRNA decay. DHRS2 exerted an anti-steatotic phenotype, and DHRS2 depletion reversed the reduction in lipid accumulation caused by LINC00885 knockdown. DHRS2 perturbation was also accompanied by changes in mitochondrial membrane potential. In a pilot serum cohort, exosomal LINC00885 and DHRS2 showed opposite expression patterns and preliminary discriminative potential. The findings support a functional LINC00885-DHRS2 axis associated with hepatocellular lipid accumulation, lipid metabolic gene expression, and mitochondrial membrane potential. The circulating exosomal observations are exploratory and require validation in larger, clinically characterized cohorts.
items.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular and cell biology of lipids
